name: General Dynamics
headline: Builds the Navy's nuclear submarines and Gulfstream jets, and gets customers to fund much of its working capital.
what_short: Submarines, Gulfstream jets, tanks and defense IT
what_it_does: General Dynamics has four parts: Marine Systems (32% of sales), which builds Navy nuclear submarines and destroyers; Aerospace (25%), which makes Gulfstream business jets; Combat Systems (17%), the sole maker of the Abrams tank and Stryker; and Technologies (26%), which does defense IT and communications.
why_it_passed: It earned about 32% before tax on the net operating capital it uses, helped by $9.8 billion of customer advances.
Electric Boat is the prime contractor and lead shipyard on all Navy nuclear-powered submarine programs, and Land Systems is the sole-source maker of the Abrams tank.
Gulfstream deliveries rose from 136 in 2024 to 158 in 2025, with orders running 1.2 times deliveries.
The Navy's long program of record, such as the 12-boat Columbia-class, gives it years of visible work.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $221 to $296 against a price of $331.72, above the top of the range. Even on the generous reading a buyer would earn about 9% a year before tax, below the roughly 10% the analysis requires.
watch: Its edge protects its place as a supplier rather than its price: segment margins sit inside its rivals' range, and the Marine margin is only 6.5% to 8.3%.
Return falls to 9.4% when the $21.0 billion of goodwill from past purchases, mostly Technologies, is counted.
Government revenue is 51% fixed-price, so cost overruns fall on the company.
